title: Tensor products commute with filtered colimits of (ring, module, module) systems
statement:
Let $I$ be a directed set, $(A_i,\alpha_{ij})_{i\in I}$ a directed system of commutative rings, and $(M_i,\mu_{ij})$, $(N_i,
u_{ij})$ directed systems of abelian groups over $I$ such that each $M_i$, $N_i$ is an $A_i$-module and the transition maps are semilinear: $\mu_{ij}(am)=\alpha_{ij}(a)\mu_{ij}(m)$, $
u_{ij}(an)=\alpha_{ij}(a)
u_{ij}(n)$ for $i\le j$. Let $A=\varinjlim A_i$, $M=\varinjlim M_i$, $N=\varinjlim N_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] with coprojections $\alpha_i,\mu_i,
u_i$, and make $M,N$ into $A$-modules by $\alpha_i(a)\mu_i(m)=\mu_i(am)$, $\alpha_i(a)
u_i(n)=
u_i(an)$ (well defined since $I$ is directed). The groups $T_i=M_i\otimes_{A_i}N_i$ form a directed system with transition maps $m\otimes n\mapsto\mu_{ij}(m)\otimes
u_{ij}(n)$ (each $T_j$ regarded as an $A_i$-module via $\alpha_{ij}$), and $T=\varinjlim T_i$ with coprojections $\lambda_i$ is an $A$-module by $\alpha_i(a)\lambda_i(t)=\lambda_i(at)$. Then there is a unique homomorphism $\psi:T	o M\otimes_AN$ with $\psi(\lambda_i(m\otimes n))=\mu_i(m)\otimes
u_i(n)$ for all $i$, $m\in M_i$, $n\in N_i$, and $\psi$ is an isomorphism of $A$-modules. Moreover $\psi$ is natural: for morphisms of such systems $(f_i:M_i	o M'_i)$, $(g_i:N_i	o N'_i)$ ($A_i$-linear, compatible with the transition maps) one has $\psi'\circ\varinjlim(f_i\otimes g_i)=(\varinjlim f_i\otimes\varinjlim g_i)\circ\psi$.

proof.text: Construct the stage balanced additive maps with TensorProduct.liftAddHom: hAM and hAN identify moving a stage scalar between the tensor factors. Compose with e_i inverse. Tensor induction and hT prove compatibility of these maps with T transitions; colimit.w identifies the M and N coprojections. The colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] produces an additive comparison p with the prescribed formula.

proof.text: Construct the inverse pairing directly. If I is empty choose zero. Otherwise Mathlib Concrete.isColimit_exists_rep and Concrete.isColimit_exists_of_rep_eq give representatives and eventual equality. To use these with arbitrary independent index and group universes, first apply AddCommGrpCat.uliftFunctor, which preserves all colimits, and shrink the filtered-colimit preservation instance of the forgetful functor. Two inputs have representatives at a common upper stage. Define their pairing to be the colimit class of the stage pure tensor. For any two presentations, find eventual equalities of the two factors and advance both to one common upper stage; functoriality and hT show equality of the tensor classes. Move three representatives to a common stage to prove additivity in each factor. Zero follows from the stage zero tensor identities.

source.place: Lemma 10.12.9 (Tag 00DD), second direct proof, adapted to varying rings; Sheaves Tag 007K is the stalk application. Source texts checked online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DD and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/007K.

proof.text: Prove scalar linearity of the pairing for every stage coefficient by moving both module inputs beyond that stage and applying hAM, hAN, hAT, smul_tmul and tmul_smul. For arbitrary coefficients, the elements of colimit A for which both scalar identities hold form a subring: zero and one use the module laws; addition and negation use additivity of the pairing; multiplication uses mul_smul twice. Every coprojection lands in this subring, so the ring colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] yields a map into the subring. The composite with the inclusion is the identity by colimit.hom_ext. Thus every coefficient belongs to this subring, proving bilinearity over colimit A. Lift this bilinear pairing using TensorProduct.lift to obtain q.

source.place: Lemma 10.12.9 (Tag 00DD), second direct proof, adapted to varying rings; Sheaves Tag 007K is the stalk application. Source texts checked online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DD and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/007K.

proof.text: Prove q p = id on the stage pure tensors. Additive maps out of a colimit are determined by coprojections even into a different universe: use the surjectivity of Colimits.Quot.desc from AddCommGrpCat.isColimit_iff_bijective_desc and Quot.addMonoidHom_ext. Tensor induction then gives the required determination by stage pure tensors. For p q = id, use tensor induction, extend the pure-tensor equality separately in each variable by this colimit extensionality, and advance the two remaining stage indices to a common upper stage. The identities give bijectivity. As q is linear and injective, applying q proves that p is linear too. Uniqueness among additive comparisons uses the same stage pure tensor extensionality. For naturality, both composites agree on these generators by hH, the comparison formula for psi prime, TensorProduct.map_tmul, hF and hG. No separate finite-relations injectivity lemma is required.
